glossary.Autoimmune: When the immune system attacks the body's own tissues.
glossary.T-cell: A lymphocyte that directs or carries out cell-mediated immune attack.
glossary.T-lymphocytes: T-cells: white blood cells driving cell-mediated immunity, here attacking myelin.
glossary.CNS: Central nervous system: the brain and spinal cord.
glossary.Myelin: Fatty insulating sheath around axons that speeds nerve conduction.
glossary.Axon: The long projection of a nerve cell that carries impulses away from the cell body.
glossary.Nerve conduction: Transmission of electrical impulses along a nerve.
glossary.Paraesthesia: Tingling, pins and needles or numbness without a stimulus.
glossary.Visual acuity: Sharpness of vision, usually tested with a Snellen chart.
glossary.Pale optic disc: A whitish optic nerve head on fundoscopy, showing optic nerve damage.
glossary.Optic disc: The point at the back of the eye where the optic nerve leaves the retina.
glossary.Cerebellar syndrome: Signs of cerebellar damage: ataxia, intention tremor, nystagmus, slurred speech, dysdiadochokinesia.
glossary.Contralateral: On the opposite side of the body.
glossary.Asymmetric: Not the same on both sides.
glossary.Lateral gaze: Looking to one side, moving both eyes horizontally.
glossary.Monophasic: A single continuous phase of illness without separate attacks.
glossary.Relapse: A new episode or flare of neurological symptoms lasting over 24 hours.
glossary.Remission: Recovery period when symptoms improve between relapses.
glossary.RRMS: Relapsing-remitting MS: attacks followed by recovery, the most common course.
glossary.PPMS: Primary progressive MS: steady worsening from onset without relapses.
glossary.Cognitive impairment: Problems with memory, attention, thinking or processing speed.
glossary.Bladder dysfunction: Problems storing or emptying urine, such as urgency, frequency or retention.
glossary.Prognosis: The likely course and outcome of a disease.
glossary.Motor signs: Signs of weakness or abnormal movement from damage to motor pathways.
glossary.Gold standard: The most accurate test available for confirming a diagnosis.
glossary.MRI: Magnetic resonance imaging: detailed scan using magnets, ideal for brain and spinal cord.
glossary.Contrast: A dye given during imaging to highlight active disease or blood vessels.
glossary.Gadolinium-enhancing: Lights up after gadolinium contrast, showing a new, active lesion with a leaky blood-brain barrier.
glossary.Hyperintensity: An area appearing brighter than surrounding tissue on MRI.
glossary.Lumbar puncture: Needle into the lower back spinal canal to sample cerebrospinal fluid.
glossary.CSF: Cerebrospinal fluid: clear fluid surrounding the brain and spinal cord.
glossary.IgG: Immunoglobulin G, the main antibody type in blood and CSF.
glossary.Ultrasound: Imaging using sound waves, quick and radiation-free.
glossary.IV: Intravenous: given directly into a vein.
glossary.Corticosteroid: Anti-inflammatory steroid drug, such as methylprednisolone, used to shorten MS relapses.
glossary.Muscle relaxants: Drugs that reduce muscle tone or spasm, such as baclofen.
glossary.Physiotherapy: Therapy using exercise and movement to keep strength, balance and mobility.
glossary.Highly active RRMS: Relapsing-remitting MS with frequent, disabling relapses despite or before treatment.
glossary.Abducens nucleus: Brainstem nucleus of cranial nerve VI, which moves the eye outwards.
glossary.Oculomotor nucleus: Brainstem nucleus of cranial nerve III, which moves the eye inwards, up and down.
glossary.Conjugate eye movements: Both eyes moving together in the same direction.
glossary.Adduction: Movement of the eye inwards towards the nose.
glossary.Abduction: Movement of the eye outwards away from the nose.
glossary.Leukocyte adhesion molecules: Surface proteins (such as alpha-4 integrin) that let white cells stick to and cross vessel walls.
glossary.Lymphocyte: A white blood cell (T-cell or B-cell) of the adaptive immune system.
glossary.Immunomodulation: Altering or damping the immune response, how DMTs work.
glossary.Relapse rate: How often relapses occur, usually counted per year.
